intervals.quote: The Homestake solar neutrino experiment was built in the period 1965–1967

intervals.label: operation
intervals.locator: Davis, Nobel Lecture 2002, p. 68, paragraph after Fig. 7
intervals.note: Start: the year Davis gives for the experiment becoming operational. The standard data set analysed by Cleveland et al. begins in 1970, when rise-time counting was introduced. The end is the end of the standard data set, not a documented shutdown: Cleveland et al. (accepted October 1997) still describe the detector as measuring solar neutrinos, and no source read dates the end of operation. The Homestake mine itself closed in 2001.
intervals.quote: The Homestake experiment became operational in 1967.

name: Homestake chlorine detector
notes: Coordinate caveat: the site referenced (site:surf-surface-campus) is a surface campus point, not the detector's true ~1478 m underground location; see placement note.

placements.note: site:surf-surface-campus is an approximate campus-level point for the whole SURF/Homestake site, used because no distinct sourced coordinate exists for the Davis chlorine-tank chamber. The detector was actually ~1478 m (4850 ft) underground, not at the surface; the placement's role is sourced from the 1998 paper, its dates from the experiment's intervals, but the site point only marks the general campus location, not the true underground depth.
placements.quote: The Homestake Solar Neutrino Observatory is located in the Homestake Gold Mine, at Lead, South Dakota

target_mass.note: Wikipedia gives the target volume (380 m³ / 100,000 gallons of perchloroethylene) but no source consulted (checked 2026-09-18) converts this to a mass; the mass is left unset rather than computed from an assumed density.

summary.plain: A tank of dry-cleaning fluid, nearly a mile underground, that turned rare chlorine atoms into argon whenever a solar neutrino struck.
summary.technical: Radiochemical chlorine-argon detector, 380 m³ perchloroethylene target, 1478 m (4850 ft) underground in the Homestake mine; built 1965-1967, operational from 1967 (standard data set 1970-1994), measured 37Ar production rate 2.56±0.16(stat)±0.16(syst) SNU.

technology.note: Reaction νe + 37Cl → 37Ar + e⁻ (inverse beta decay) and the extraction/counting steps: Cleveland et al. 1998 abstract (src:homestake-1998-flux-measurement). Perchloroethylene tank, argon extraction by helium sweep every two to three months: Davis Nobel lecture (quoted). The 'dry-cleaning fluid' gloss is from Wikipedia.
technology.quote: build a 100,000-gallon chlorine-argon neutrino detector in the Homestake Gold Mine ... In order to extract argon from the tank, helium is bubbled through the perchloroethylene.
technology.value: Radiochemical chlorine detector: solar neutrinos capture on 37Cl to produce 37Ar via inverse beta decay in a large tank of perchloroethylene (dry-cleaning fluid), with the argon periodically extracted and counted
